correctness.rationale: In the one-edge BA tree, summing endpoint depths over edges gives 2P_n-(n-1). The parent-depth conditional mean is therefore P_n/(n-1)-1/2; multiplying parent depth by the root-attachment indicator gives zero. Iterating the expectation recurrences gives m_n=E R_n as the stated gamma ratio and E P_n=(n-1)(H_{n-1}+1)/2. The covariance recurrence is c_{n+1}=(1+3/[2(n-1)])c_n-m_n H_{n-1}/[4(n-1)]. Dividing by m_{n+1}(2n+1) telescopes to the strictly positive B_n sum with c_2=0. Its harmonic form follows by expanding H_{k-1} and telescoping the partial fractions; the harmonic difference tends to -log 2. Dividing covariance by m_n gives the shift exactly, with no stochastic-order claim. As another check, weighting histories by R_n/m_n changes each transition to degree weights with just one extra unit at the root, and denominator 2n-1; this follows by telescoping the degree ratio along the root attachments. The tilted mean then satisfies p*_{n+1}=((2n+1)p*_n+n)/(2n-1), consistent with p*_n=E P_n-B_n. Independent exact weighting of 5,913 histories through n=8 verified both means, both forms of B_n and covariance (at n=8, -169549/40960); /workspace/branches/7ba111e7-f280-4901-a6d6-ae31187eb286/replay_record2.py and replay_n8.txt. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed. Finite replay is supplementary.

value.rationale: Comparing the first hub with a natural global depth statistic is different from comparing its degree to the leaf count or observing short mean pairwise distances. The exact finite-size shift is a quantitative benchmark for selection proportional to hub degree: it has a strict sign at every nontrivial size and a linear leading cost with a specified coefficient. Neither the sign nor the coefficient follows from the marginal means, and the result does not overstate an ordering of the two laws.
